summary: Makera Carvera desktop CNC mill: 360 × 240 × 140 mm, 200 W spindle to 15 000 rev/min, 6-slot automatic tool changer, built-in 2.5 W laser.

options.summary: With Makera's 4th-axis module: a continuous A rotary along X taking stock up to Ø92 × 240 mm.

sources.from: Makera's Carvera specification page (Spindle, Motion System, Dimensions)
Makera's published specifications for the Carvera (makera.com product and specification pages, retailer specification sheets) and the Carvera community documentation
Makera's published specifications for the Carvera 4th-axis module
Makera's collets for this machine: 1/8" (standard), 1/4", 6, 4 and 3 mm (confirmed by the user)
Makera's buying guides (Z1 vs Z1 Pro; Carvera vs Carvera Air) and the UNSW Making Carvera guide

notes: The control measures each tool's length after a change, so programs carry no tool length offset (the makera post).
The 1/8" collet is standard; the others are optional collets.
Motion: servo motors on X, Y and Z (400 W in all), 15 mm linear rails and ball screws on X and Z, 25 mm hardened rods and a ball screw on Y.
Spindle runout under 0.01 mm; resolution 0.01 mm.

Makera's starting feeds (manual p54): aluminium and copper 0.1–0.2 mm deep, 300–500 mm/min, 200 mm/min plunge, 12 000 rev/min with a single-flute bit for metal; wood and plastic 0.5–2 mm deep, 500–1000 mm/min at 10 000 rev/min. Heavier cuts are the programmer's choice: the generate notice estimates each roughing operation's spindle load.
Workholding (manual p45): L-brackets with top clamps for stock under 20 mm, side clamps on the thick bracket above that; a 1–2 mm waste board under through cuts.
The work origin is set from anchor 1 (lower left) or anchor 2; machine zero is the upper right (manual p26, p31).
Jogging runs at the G0 speed, 3000 mm/min by default (manual p35).
Programs call tools T1–T6 with M6 (the wireless probe is the seventh); any other number stops with an alarm (manual p27, p36).
